subject: TEST
subtopic: Rational numbers as a subset of real numbers
axis_note: Three draft reconstruction rungs from an independently custody-READY NCERT Q1. Not canonical curriculum.

must_contain: Recognise a/b with integers a,b and b ≠ 0.
Give a nonintegral rational example, such as 1/2.
Refute natural/integer/whole as universal categories using counterexamples.

controlled_variation.notice: Rational is not synonymous with integer or natural number.

must_contain: Explain why every rational is real.
Counterexample √2 disproves the reverse claim that every real is rational.

family.invariant_demand: Classify a number by the smallest supported set claims without reversing set inclusion.
family.difficult_move: Distinguish every rational is real from every real is rational.
family.independent_check: Use a fractional rational and an irrational real counterexample.

support_ladder.handed_over: The inclusion Q ⊆ R and the rational definition.
The two set names, but not which contains which.
Only the source MCQ and the requirement to justify every option.

transfer.changed_demand: Given a new rational, decide which set-membership statements hold universally.
Challenge the reverse inclusion using one irrational real number.
